citations.text: Efklides, A., & Schwartz, B. L. (2024). Revisiting the Metacognitive and Affective Model of Self-Regulated Learning: Origins, Development, and Future Directions. Educational Psychology Review, 36, 61.

en.general: Three levels in the Enriched Model of Metacognition that MASRL builds on: an object level of nonconscious thinking with its own monitoring and control, a Personal Awareness level where the person becomes conscious of feelings and judgments about it, and a Social level for co-regulation, where feelings cannot be shared directly but can be perceived and judged. The article does not say how these levels line up with MASRL's Person and Task X Person levels.

examples: Retrieving an answer with low confidence and quietly deciding not to give it (object level).
A student noticing a tip-of-the-tongue state (Personal Awareness level).

labels.en: Object Level, Personal Awareness Level and Social Level (Enriched Model)

nonExamples: A student quietly judging her own answer with no one else involved (Personal Awareness level, which differs from the Social level).
A student's belief that effort pays off (a Person-level characteristic in MASRL).
